items.title: City to buy United Church with over 130-year history in Mississauga
items.summary: A church with an over 130-year history in Mississauga could be city property. The United Church at 151 Lakeshore Rd. W. in Port Credit is listed for sale, and the City of Mississauga is in the process of buying it, a city spokesperson told INSAUGA Canada this week. In July, then-Mayor Carolyn Parrish announced the city had plans to buy the church and use it as an event venue and permanent home for the Canada Virtuoso Ensemble. ca for nearly six months. Most recently known as the Christ First United Church, the church amalgamated with the Clarkson Christ First United Church at 1700 Mazo Cres. in 2019, Christ First United Church spokesperson Janis Cowie told INSAUGA Canada. They moved services to the Clarkson church in 2019, and haven’t held regular services in Port Credit since then. They are, however, planning a Candlelight Service in the Port Credit church on Sunday, Dec. m. “On normal Sundays, a Spanish church holds services in Port Credit,” the spokesperson said. The interior of the Christ First United Church in Port Credit.

items.title: Stay away from rivers and streams in Mississauga, Brampton and elsewhere: CVC
items.summary: Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon residents are being warned to stay away from all watercourses in the next couple of days, particularly at and near the Credit River, as widespread rainfall could cause dangerous conditions. Credit Valley Conservation, the organization that protects natural areas and watercourses in Peel’s three municipalities and several other communities, issued a water safety statement on Thursday morning alerting people to potentially unsafe conditions due to the heavy rainfall heading to southern Ontario. The statement, which remains in effect until end of day on Sunday, noted an approaching low-pressure system is expected to bring rainfall amounts exceeding 30 mm to the area by Saturday, including the possibility of freezing rain in the Upper Credit River watershed. “The Credit River watershed did not receive any rain during the last 10 days, so soil is dry and water levels in watercourses are low,” CVC said in its statement. “Flooding of the Credit River and its major tributaries is not expected. However, some watersheds may respond with higher flows and water levels. As a result, local streams and rivers may become unsafe, especially in the vicinity of culverts, bridges and dams. ” Conservation authority officials added they’ll continue to closely monitor the weather and water levels in the watershed and will update residents with any new information or alerts. CVC officials said a water safety statement is issued when high flows, unsafe banks, melting ice or other factors could be dangerous for recreational users such as anglers, canoeists, hikers, children and pets. WATER SAFETY STATEMENT: Widespread rainfall is expected starting today, into Saturday. Flooding is not expected. For safety, keep children and pets aways from watercourses.

items.title: Mississauga restaurant ordered to temporarily close during health inspection
items.summary: The restaurant and bakery on Dundas Street was inspected by Peel Public Health officials Nov. 25. Peel Public Health provides the public with information about inspections of food establishments in the region. Peel Public Health officials temporarily closed a Mississauga restaurant during a recent inspection. Inspectors routinely check local restaurants, cocktail bars/beverage rooms, bakeries and takeout food establishments to ensure compliance with food safety standards. Revrea’s Grill & Bakeshop, a restaurant and bakery at 1057 Dundas St. , was ordered to close when it was inspected Nov. 25. items.title: Man charged in string of home invasions targeting luxury cars in Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: , faces dozens of charges over five home invasions that took place between May 29 and June 2, Peel police said Thursday. Peel police announced they have made an arrest in five home invasions earlier this year in the Toronto region. A man who was already in custody has been charged in connection with several Toronto region home invasions targeting luxury vehicles that occurred within a week earlier this year. , faces dozens of charges in five home invasions in Toronto, Brampton and Mississauga that happened between May 29 and June 2. Peel police believe all of them to be connected and carried out by the same group of three or four suspects, investigators announced on Thursday. The investigation is ongoing and police expect to make more arrests, they said. Suspects forcibly entered residences in the early morning hours and demanded vehicle keys from occupants, police said, adding that several luxury vehicles, including BMW and Mercedes models, were stolen or targeted. None of the victims were physically injured, according to investigators. Police in Toronto and Peel Region subsequently co-ordinated on a probe dubbed “Project Twilight,” and arrested the man and a 20-year-old woman from Hamilton on June 8. However, investigators now don’t believe the woman was involved in the home invasions, Det. Cst. Nathan Ball said at a news conference Thursday.

items.title: Mississauga Real Estate Agent Joe Battaglia Wins 2026 Readers' Choice Diamond
items.summary: There were 1,333 press releases posted in the last 24 hours and 505,676 in the last 365 days. Joe Battaglia, Broker of Record of the #39 ranked REMAX Small Residential Team in Canada. , was Voted for Best Real Estate Agent in Mississauga in the 2026 Readers' Choice Awards presented by The Mississauga News. Joe Battaglia, a Mississauga real estate agent with REMAX Realty Specialists, received the Diamond award, the program's top community-voted ranking. , has been awarded Diamond status in the Best Real Estate Agent category of the 2026 Best of Mississauga Readers' Choice Awards. Diamond is the highest of the program's three placements, awarded to the business receiving the most votes in its category. The Readers' Choice Community Business Awards program is operated by Metroland Media Group Ltd. and runs across dozens of Ontario communities. Its outcome is determined entirely by the public. Residents nominate businesses in their own community, the five most-nominated businesses in each category advance to a voting round, and the three finishing highest are ranked Diamond, Platinum and Gold. No panel, jury or paid entry is involved at any stage, and Metroland reports the program draws more than 70,000 nominations and over half a million votes each year. That structure is what distinguishes the result from industry recognition. Most real estate awards measure sales volume or transaction counts, which reward scale. A community vote measures something else entirely: how many people were willing to put a name forward and return weeks later to vote for it.

items.title: How close is the Hurontario LRT to being finished?
items.summary: The Hurontario LRT, also known as the Hazel McCallion Line, was supposed to be completed in the fall of 2024, but the pandemic and construction delays prevented that from happening. CBC’s Nav Nanwa updates us on the project and how close it is to completion.

items.title: Community outrage sparks judicial review of Mississauga cannabis store licence
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is seeking a judicial review of the province's decision to grant a retail licence to a cannabis store in Meadowvale Village, following backlash from residents who say they weren't consulted about it.

items.title: Peel Police Set to Detail New Home Invasion Probe Tied to Luxury Vehicle Thefts
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel police are set to release details of a new probe into home invasions across the GTA targeting luxury vehicles. Investigators say auto theft has dropped in Mississauga and Brampton in recent years, but it remains a top concern, especially when a home break-in is involved, since that puts residents at risk. The announcement follows a separate bust less than two weeks ago in which a dozen men face 231 combined charges over stolen luxury SUVs and other high-value vehicles taken from driveways across the GTA. Police say that ring moved the stolen vehicles out of Ontario within days, loading them into containers bound overseas from the Port of Montreal. The probe, led by Peel's commercial auto crime squad with the Canada Border Services Agency, turned up a broader criminal network across the region, investigators said.

items.title: Mississauga Councillor Says Malton Greenway Sees Eight Encampment Removals a Month
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga council voted unanimously on Nov. 25 to study improvements for the Malton Greenway after Ward 5 Coun. Natalie Hart said years of neglect and encampments have left residents afraid to use the trail. Hart told council and city staff that the two-kilometre park and trail in the city's north end is meant to connect people but currently cannot be used safely. She said the area has seen more encampments than resident activity over the past couple of years, with crews now removing roughly eight encampments a month. Hart's motion directs city staff to explore options for cleaning up and improving safety along the greenway. The councillor pointed to an incident the same morning in which a parks crew was called to clear garbage illegally dumped behind a nearby mall.
